newsitem.title: USA: Betty Shabazz undergoes more skin surgery.
newsitem.headline: Betty Shabazz undergoes more skin surgery.

text.p: The widow of Malcolm X, badly burned in a fire allegedly set by her troubled grandson, underwent a fourth surgical procedure on Sunday to remove more of her charred skin, hospital officials said.
"Her condition remained stable throughout the procedure and she tolerated the surgery very well," a hospital spokeswoman said.
"To date, the burn team has removed 72 percent of the burned tissue," she said.

Sunday's procedure began at 8 a.m EDT and Shabazz was returned to the burn unit at the Jacobi Hospital in the New York City borough of the Bronx about 3 p.m. EDT, the spokeswoman said. The next procedure will be performed on Tuesday, she said.
Shabazz's burned skin is replaced with Integra, an artificial skin product. The material lets the inner layer of her skin to heal enough to accept a permanent graft later.

Shabazz, 63, suffered third-degree burns over 80 percent of her body in a fire last Sunday at her Yonkers, New York, co-op apartment. A third-degree burn is one that extends deep into the skin's underlying tissue.

Malcolm Shabazz, 12, who is named after his grandfather, Malcolm X, is alleged to have splashed fuel at the door of his grandmother's apartment and set it afire. Shabazz's nylon nightgown caught fire and "she went up in flames" when she tried to put the blaze out, family friends said.

The child was being held at a juvenile facility awaiting his next date in Family Court. He was the son of Qubilah Shabazz, 36, charged in the 1995 plot to kill Nation of Islam leader Louis Farrakhan because she believed he was responsible for her father's 1965 assassination.
